name: Slate
_comment: A stylesheet as data. Each key is a selector; each rule may carry `font`, `color`, `bg`, `border` and `pad`.
`face` is a built-in name (sans / serif / mono / fraktur) or a path to a font THIS addon ships
("fonts/Inter.ttf"), which main.lua maps through hafen.asset. `size` is logical px; omit it and the
surface keeps its own stock size, which is what stops a theme from moving the layout.
A border's `image` is a path to a file this addon ships and is mapped the same way, because an image is a
HANDLE: those two are the only values JSON cannot carry -- a colour, a slice and a pad are already the
sheet's own shape and travel verbatim.
No colour on window.title / heading / a plain button caption: those surfaces are EMBOSSED (a texture is
tiled through the glyph mask), so a colour rule there is inert -- see docs/addons/api/ui.md#what-each-key-accepts.
window.frame is the window CHROME and panel the framed surfaces that are NOT windows; both draw and
neither writes, so they take bg/border/pad and no font or colour. A panel cannot re-lay itself out, so it
takes no pad and its art is drawn into the ~5 px the stock box had -- hence the thin panel.png beside the
window's frame.png, whose 40 px top inset is the title band the caption sits in (a smaller one would put
the caption over the content: the engine adds no hidden room for it).
The last three rules say WHERE, not what: a selector that names a window may carry `anchor` (a corner of
the screen or of another widget, plus an offset in raw pixels), or `pos`/`size` as plain [x, y] arrays.
Nothing about them is mapped -- they are already the sheet's own shapes -- so the layout half of this
theme cost main.lua not one line. A window with no rule keeps the place its user gave it, and dropping
the sheet puts every window back where it was, to the pixel.
An anchor HOLDS (it is re-derived whenever the screen or its target changes, so dragging an anchored
window snaps back). ':theme save' pins each of them at where it is now instead, through hafen.store --
the demonstration that a layout PROFILE is an addon's own business and not an engine feature.
